raw_meta_yaml:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prefix-dev/recipe-format/main/schema.json
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "50.0.1"
  build_number: 1

recipe:
  name: cryptography-split
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/pyca/cryptography/archive/refs/tags/${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 649f6cfd4c9988e85adc3b480479d7e36f43f8e4861cac0e0c7fc68b45dd7075

build:
  number: ${{ build_number }}
  skip:
    # relocation errors
    - ppc64le
    # todo: segfaults for unknown reason
    - linux and aarch64 and is_freethreading
    - is_abi3 and not is_python_min

outputs:
  - package:
      name: cryptography-vectors
    build:
      # this is noarch, but building it in a different feedstock from the same
      # sources just causes every single upgrade PR to fail pointlessly, so we
      # build it here (only one build will be uploaded due to coinciding hashes)
      noarch: python
      script: python -m pip install ./vectors -vv --no-build-isolation
      # avoid build hash which includes subdir-specific `python_min`
      string: noarch_${{ build_number }}
    requirements:
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - uv-build
        - pip
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - cryptography_vectors
          pip_check: true
          python_version:
            - ${{ python_min }}.*
            - "*"
    about:
      license: BSD-3-Clause OR Apache-2.0
      license_file:
        - LICENSE
        - LICENSE.BSD
        - LICENSE.APACHE
      summary: Test vectors for the cryptography package.
      homepage: https://pypi.org/project/cryptography-vectors
      repository: https://github.com/pyca/cryptography/tree/main/vectors

  - package:
      name: cryptography
    build:
      python:
        version_independent: ${{ is_abi3 }}
      script:
        env:
          # see below for what OPENSSL_DIR should be pointing to:
          # https://github.com/sfackler/rust-openssl/blob/openssl-sys-v0.9.72/openssl/src/lib.rs#L55-L56
          OPENSSL_DIR: ${{ "$PREFIX" if unix else "%LIBRARY_PREFIX%" }}
          CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_STRIP: symbols
          CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO: fat
          CARGO: cargo-auditable-wrapper.${{ "bat" if win else "sh" }}
        content:
          - if: win
            then:
              - copy "%RECIPE_DIR%\cargo-auditable-wrapper.bat" "%BUILD_PREFIX%\Library\bin\"
            else:
              - cp "${RECIPE_DIR}/cargo-auditable-wrapper.sh" "${BUILD_PREFIX}/bin/"
              - chmod 755 "${BUILD_PREFIX}/bin/cargo-auditable-wrapper.sh"
          - python -m pip install . -vv --no-build-isolation
          - cargo-bundle-licenses --format yaml --output THIRDPARTY.yml
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler("c") }}
        - ${{ compiler("rust") }}
        - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
        - cargo-auditable
        - cargo-bundle-licenses
        - if: build_platform != target_platform
          then:
            - cffi >=2.0
            - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
            - maturin >=1,<2
            - python
      host:
        - cffi >=2.0
        - maturin >=1,<2
        - openssl
        - pip
        - python
        # used by cffi
        - setuptools
        - if: win and is_freethreading
          then:
            # force stubborn solver to play ball
            - python >=3.14.1
        - if: is_abi3
          then:
            - python-abi3
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*
      run:
        - python
        - cffi >=2.0
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - cryptography
            - cryptography.fernet
            - cryptography.hazmat
            - cryptography.hazmat.backends
            - cryptography.hazmat.backends.openssl
            - cryptography.hazmat.bindings
            - cryptography.hazmat.bindings.openssl
            - cryptography.hazmat.primitives
            - cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric
            - cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers
            - cryptography.hazmat.primitives.kdf
            - cryptography.hazmat.primitives.twofactor
            - cryptography.x509
          pip_check: true
          python_version:
            - "*"
            - if: is_abi3
              then:
                - ${{ python_min }}.*
      - if: is_abi3
        then:
          - files:
              recipe:
                # run_test.py will check that the correct openssl version is linked
                - run_test.py
            requirements:
              run:
                - abi3audit
                - python ${{ python_min }}.*
            script:
              - python run_test.py
              - cd "${{ "$SP_DIR" if unix else "%SP_DIR%" }}/cryptography/hazmat/bindings"
              - abi3audit -s -v --assume-minimum-abi3 ${{ python_min }} _rust.${{ "abi3.so" if unix else "pyd" }}
      - files:
          recipe:
            # run_test.py will check that the correct openssl version is linked
            - run_test.py
          source:
            - tests/
            # for marker definitions
            - pyproject.toml
        requirements:
          run:
            - certifi
            - cryptography-vectors ${{ version }}.*
            - hypothesis
            - iso8601
            - pretend
            - pytest
            # needs to avoid newest version due to https://github.com/conda-forge/py-cpuinfo-feedstock/issues/11
            - pytest-benchmark <5.3
            - pytest-subtests
            - pytz
        script:
          - python run_test.py
          - pytest tests

about:
  license: Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause AND PSF-2.0 AND MIT
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
    - THIRDPARTY.yml
  summary: cryptography is a package designed to expose cryptographic primitives and recipes to Python developers.
  homepage: https://pypi.org/project/cryptography
  repository: https://github.com/pyca/cryptography
  documentation: https://cryptography.io
  description: |
    cryptography is a package which provides cryptographic recipes and
    primitives to Python developers. Our goal is for it to be your
    "cryptographic standard library". It supports Python 3.6+ and PyPy3 7.2+.
    cryptography includes both high level recipes and low level interfaces
    to common cryptographic algorithms such as symmetric ciphers, message
    digests, and key derivation functions.
